plan.angle: Title: 'Tirzepatide vs Semaglutide: Which Had More Stomach Side Effects?' Answer by 10 s: 'In SURMOUNT-5, stomach side effects were about as common on both.' Then nausea, diarrhoea, constipation and vomiting rates per arm, plus GI-related stopping rates per arm, all from NEJM, with group sizes. Say side effects weren't a formally tested comparison. Population: adults with obesity, no diabetes, 72 weeks, open-label, Lilly-funded. 2 recommended habits (smaller meals eaten slowly; fluids unless you've been told to limit fluids). 'Don't switch or stop on your own.' Prescriber line.
plan.working_title: Tirzepatide vs Semaglutide: Which Had More Stomach Side Effects? #shorts
plan.why: A follow-up to the 109-view SURMOUNT-5 head-to-head. It names both drugs with tirzepatide first, and it's the strongest bet for the 08:00 slot. | fact-check: Good, data-backed head-to-head (SURMOUNT-5, Aronne et al., NEJM 2025; 72 wk; adults with obesity without diabetes; open-label; Lilly-sponsored; max tolerated doses). The stomach side-effect rates were broadly SIMILAR between arms. Secondary summaries report roughly nausea 44% vs 44%, diarrhoea 23% vs 23%, constipation 27% vs 29%, and vomiting 15% on tirzepatide vs 21% on semaglutide. Do NOT use these secondary numbers: take every rate and the GI-discontinuation rates (with group sizes, ~374 vs ~376) directly from the NEJM paper or its supplement. Adverse events were not a formally tested endpoint. The title question must be answered honestly as 'about the same overall', with no claim that one drug is 'gentler' or 'better tolerated'. Vomiting can be mentioned only as a numerical difference, not a tested one. Note the timing (mostly during dose escalation) only if the paper says so. Habits are fine as 'recommended', with the fluid caveat. Keep 'Don't switch or stop on your own'.

package.title: Tirzepatide vs Semaglutide: More Stomach Side Effects? #shorts
package.description:
In SURMOUNT-5 (adults with obesity or overweight plus a weight-related condition, no diabetes; 72 weeks; 374 on tirzepatide vs 376 on semaglutide, highest tolerated doses): nausea (~44%) and diarrhea (~23%) were about the same. Vomiting (~15% tirzepatide vs ~21% semaglutide) and stopping for stomach side effects (~3% vs ~6%) were numerically lower with tirzepatide, but weren't formally compared, so the gap isn't proven.

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

Sources:
1. Aronne LJ et al., SURMOUNT-5, N Engl J Med 2025;393:26-36 — https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2416394
2. Gorgojo-Martínez JJ et al., J Clin Med 2022;12(1):145 — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9821052/
3. SURMOUNT-5, NCT05822830 — https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05822830
4. SURMOUNT-5 Journal Scan, ACC, 2025 — https://www.acc.org/Latest-in-Cardiology/Journal-Scans/2025/07/10/09/09/SURMOUNT-5

Tirzepatide vs semaglutide: which one gave more stomach side effects? In SURMOUNT-5 (adults with obesity or overweight plus a weight-related condition, no diabetes), mostly about the same.

Over 72 weeks — 374 on tirzepatide vs 376 on semaglutide, at their highest tolerated doses:
• Nausea: ~44% in each group
• Diarrhea: ~23% in each group
• Constipation: ~27% vs ~28%
• Vomiting: ~15% tirzepatide vs ~21% semaglutide, and stopping due to stomach side effects: ~3% vs ~6% — but these weren't formally compared, so that gap isn't proven

Most effects were mild to moderate, mainly during dose increases.

factcheck.summary: The SURMOUNT-5 side-effect Short is accurate, balanced and safe. Group sizes, population, timeframe, design and funding are stated correctly in the narration. The per-arm numbers I could check match the published results within rounding: nausea 43.6% vs 44.4%, diarrhoea 23.5% vs 23.4%, constipation 27.0% vs 28.5%, vomiting 15.0% vs 21.3%. The ACC Journal Scan confirms that 2.7% vs 5.6% stopped because of stomach side effects, and that most events were mild to moderate and happened during dose escalation. Framing the vomiting and stopping gaps as "not formally compared" is honest. The fluids tip keeps its caveat, and the "don't switch or stop on your own" line plus the prescriber line are both there. I list two minor wording fixes. The NEJM, PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov and PMC pages block automated access, so I couldn't open them directly. I confirmed the NEJM paper's numbers through secondary reports, and the PMC paper's existence and scope through its index listings.

issues.claim: Constipation: about 27% on tirzepatide versus about 28% on semaglutide.
issues.problem: The reported semaglutide figure is 28.5%, which rounds to 29%, not 28%. It's a small understatement, but the number should match the source.
issues.fix: Narration: "Constipation: about 27% on tirzepatide versus about 29% on semaglutide." Keep any on-screen or list text matching ("~27% vs ~29%").

issues.problem: The on-screen text drops the trial context. Without it, the line reads as a general claim about the two drugs rather than a SURMOUNT-5 result, and vomiting did differ numerically.

audio.soundNotes: Measured music levels (-13.5 dB under voice, -14.7 in pauses) already sit inside target, so left music_gain at 1.0. Cleaned up redundant doubled cues firing at the same timestamp (swell+whoosh, swoosh+tick, pop+whip, pop+whoosh pairs) by zeroing one of each pair to keep density within the 3-4/second ceiling and avoid clutter. Pulled back the i36 swell (was -11.5 dB rel. voice, too loud under speech at the "~15% vs ~21%" stat) by about 3 dB, and lifted the i5 pop (was -14.7 dB, too quiet for the pause at the whip transition after "About the same") by about 3 dB so transitions still land. Added two bespoke accents: a resolving twin-tone chime on the "about the same" reveal and a soft water-sip sound under the fluids tip, both kept low since the first lands in a pause and the second under speech.
